recipes.name: Homemade Pastrami
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup coarsely ground fresh black pepper

steps.text: Mix vegetable oil and garlic in a small bowl; set aside for 1 hour. Combine black pepper, paprika, coriander, dry mustard, white pepper, and cayenne pepper in a large bowl; set aside.
Preheat the oven to 225 degrees F (110 degrees C).

Cover a baking sheet with a large sheet of heavy-duty aluminum foil; coat with prepared garlic oil. Lay beef brisket on the oiled foil sheet and brush with remaining garlic oil. Cover brisket completely with pepper mixture, reserving 1 to 2 tablespoons.

Wrap brisket, fat-side up, in the sheet of foil. Place wrapped corned beef on another sheet of aluminum foil with the seam- and fat-sides down. Place double-wrapped brisket, seam-side down, on a third sheet of aluminum foil; wrap again.
Bake in the preheated oven for 6 hours.
Remove pastrami from the oven and let cool to room temperature, about 3 hours. Do not remove the foil.
Place foil-wrapped pastrami in a freezer bag or other plastic bag; refrigerate for 8 to 10 hours.
Preheat the oven's broiler and set the oven rack about 6 inches from the heat source. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
Remove pastrami from the refrigerator, unwrap, and place on the prepared baking sheet. Sprinkle top with 1 to 2 tablespoons remaining pepper mixture.
Place pastrami under the broiler and cook until surface browns, 3 to 4 minutes. Remove pastrami from the oven and cut into thin slices, about 1/8-inch thick.
Heat a large skillet over low heat; warm pastrami slices in the skillet with a few drops of water until fat turns translucent, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Pastrami
raw_recipe.description: Make delicious pastrami at home with brisket using Chef John's recipe for spicy, intensely aromatic pastrami that is easy to make without a smoker.

review.reviewBody: This was really, REALLY good. It was not hard at all, even though there were a lot of steps. Once I applied the rub, it was just a matter of triple-sealing the meat. The number of steps just looks intimidating. Mine came out a nice dark pink. I bought a rectangular shaped corned beef for even slices, which I recommend. My meat was also leaner than the meat in the video. I was able to trim most of the visisble fat.

I’m making my 4th batch of this pastrami. I even have people ask when I’m making it again. Everyone loves it. I made one change now - I do 4 hours in the smoker and 2 hours wrapped in foil in the oven. OMG! Chef John this is a great recipe

My first attempt wasn't so great- the foil leaked, it was too peppery/spicy (but ironically lacked flavor) and the topping turned into a gooey mess. Second attempt- I used half the black pepper, eliminated the cayenne pepper, added a tablespoon of brown sugar and increased the garlic cloves to 4. Then I marinated the meat in the oil/garlic overnight. I made sure to use larger pieces of foil and wrapped it much tighter. I also added a fourth wrap. Beyond that, I followed the directions and it came out much better although I still had to scrape off some of the topping. The best part of this recipe is the idea of reheating it in a frying pan with a bit of water, that's a requirement. I'm going to try one more time and see if I can get this up to 5 stars.

My hubby and I love going to Deli's and eating pastrami. We want to say Thank You Chef John for this recipe we love it. We Made it twice now and is now going to be a staple in our house. My husband and I left out Cayenne this last time and that took away from the heat. We are wimps when it comes to to much spicy food so it turned out perfect. Plus we put it on our Pit Boss to Smoke that baby up. If you can Highly Suggest smoking it for at least an hour.

I just cooked this recipe for the third time and I will cook it again soon! 

Changes: 3 cloves of garlic and shorter cooking time. I prefer strong a strong garlic taste and I found that cooking it for about 5-5.5 hours - instead of 6 - resulted in a more tender, rare pastrami. 5 stars!
Pretty good flavor on its own but the smoked paprika wasn't giving it enough of a smoky flavor. I will be adding 1/2 teaspoon on liquid smoke to the oil, garlic rub nest to up that smokey flavor.

This was really, really good. Am making again with a few changes. First, Cut off most of the fat first, then apply the rub. Otherwise you cut off that great flavor afterwards. Second, I will apply the rub & let sit for 24 hours before cooking. Can’t wait!!!

I made this from home made corned beef. It is spectacular. Mine was a bit salty, but I discovered the issue was I didn’t soak the corn beef before turning into pastrami. I like spice so I doubled the cayenne and added a bit extra smoked paprika. It’s the closet the deli pastrami from nyc Ive ever had. I did not have liquid smoke and I don’t think I would add it. Next time I think the smoked paprika was sufficient. And I’m a fan of smoked. I have another brisket brining recipe turned out so well this time I’m going to follow the spices exactly so I can share it with more people. Not so spicy. Although there are a lot of steps to this recipe, it is extremely simple part of the reason it’s so simple as it’s written in such clear steps.

I followed the instructions and then I added a half a capful of liquid smoke to the oil and garlic. Just a little bit gave me the smoky flavour of a pit bbq Smoked for 8 hours!!
Excellent is all I can say
So easy and the some of the best pastrami. I soak the corned beef for 2 hours in water so it is not so salty. I add pastrami crumble to scrambled eggs or an omelet for extra special eggs.

Absolutely AWESOME!! I added 1 tbsp. of ginger to the rub the second time I made it. LOL, when I mention that I am making my pastrami neighborly visits seem to pick up. I have a small kitchen slicer that I use, then vacuum seal 5 slices (2 sandwich worth) per short bag and freeze it. A 4lb. corned beef brisket yields about 8 bags (plus a sandwich or 2). You will not regret the time this recipe takes and your local deli may be short a pastrami customer.

This is definitely a keeper and will be making this again soon. The meat is so tender. Next time I will reduce the amount of pepper and add garlic powder and brown sugar to the spice mixture. I didn't have smoked paprika used regular but will definitely use the smoked next time.
It takes a while but is so easy and so good.
Will never go out again unless its Katz Deli

OMG! This is crazy good! The video really helped make this a definite keeper. Not as hard as it might seem at first glance. YOU must try it! So… made this incredibly delicious pastrami again. I cooked 2 at the same time and cheated a bit by using premade pickling spice. Cooked 2 that we could slice and place portions in freezer bags to have on hand for Football Sundays!
Great flavor. Perfect for grilled reubens sandwiches! This recipe is definitely a keeper!
It is the easiest way to make real tasting pastrami!
Incredible! Start the day before. I’ve made this six times and it’s great!
